inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 annual report cash flow statement 'Share-based payments' add-back $111M (TRI.TO_Annual_FY2025.txt:7554) plus $16M 'Other financing activities', used as the proxy for cash withholding tax on net-settled awards (note 25 says contributed-surplus movements include those payments; TRI publishes no combined figure). H1 2026 SBC $70M on $4,041M revenue = 1.73%.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows are in USD; TRI.TO quotes in CAD on the TSX. Per-share values are computed in USD and converted at USD/CAD 1.4254 (Yahoo USDCAD=X, 2026-10-10T04:21Z). Parity check against the Nasdaq listing: TRI US$103.21 x 1.4254 = C$147.12 vs TRI.TO C$147.30 observed at the same 2026-10-09 close, a 0.12% tie that confirms the rate, its direction and the quote basis. refresh_price.py does not move fx_rate, so re-date this if the price is refreshed much later.
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 433,224,578 common shares outstanding at 4 Aug 2026 (Q2 2026 MD&A, TRI.TO_Quarterly_Q2-2026.txt:1393), which already reflects the May 2026 share consolidation (~6.5M shares removed) and the July 2026 buyback of 2.6M shares, plus 2.2M TRSUs/PRSUs and ~0.5M treasury-method shares for the 2.05M options outstanding = 435.9M. Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows. The Metrics.csv shares_outstanding column is sparse and annual-only; the Q2 2026 diluted weighted average of 438.6M is not used because it includes about a month before the consolidation.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD-built rate. 10-year UST ~4.3%, 5-year beta ~0.85 for a 81%-recurring subscription business, ERP 5.0% gives cost of equity ~8.55%; debt is ~6% of EV at ~4.8% pre-tax (commercial paper plus notes). That puts WACC at ~8.3%, rounded up to 8.5% for the Woodbridge (~70%) control and Founders Share constraints on minority holders. AI-disruption risk is charged in the scenario flows (bear growth/margin path and a 25% bear weight), NOT in the discount rate: the same 8.5% is used in every scenario so the risk is charged once.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as an operating cost. FY2025 lease cash cost $78M (principal $64M at TRI.TO_Annual_FY2025.txt:6374 plus lease interest $14M at :7634) = 1.1% of ex-Print revenue, deducted via lease_cost_pct_path, gliding to 0.8% as revenue grows against a flat footprint. Lease liabilities ($241M at 30 Jun 2026) are EXCLUDED from net_debt, so net_debt here is lower than the company's own 'net debt' figure ($2,628M), which adds leases. D&A for the tax line is taken ex right-of-use depreciation.
inputs.nci_treatment: No material NCI (the last $384M NCI purchase was in 2024; NCI lines are nil in FY2025). Flows are 100% attributable.
inputs.global_print_treatment: Global Print (FY2025 revenue $490M, segment EBITDA $185M at 37.7%; TRI.TO_Annual_FY2025.txt:4887) is carved OUT of the forward flows: 51% is being sold to a KKR-advised JV for ~$500M gross, closing Q4 2026, and it becomes a discontinued operation at Q3 2026. base_revenue = FY2025 total $7,476M less Global Print $490M = $6,986M. Its value enters the equity bridge instead (net proceeds plus the retained 49%), and the minimum-return backstop to KKR is a reason to haircut the retained stake. Management says deconsolidation adds 60-70bp to total organic growth with minimal margin impact; ex-Print adjusted EBITDA margin in FY2025 was ($2,936M - $185M)/$6,986M = 39.4%, essentially the total-company 39.2%.
inputs.ebitda_basis: TRI's adjusted EBITDA does NOT add back share-based payments (the reconciliation at TRI.TO_Annual_FY2025.txt:4599 removes only amortization, fair-value adjustments, other operating gains, finance costs and tax). So it is already post-SBC. The engine deducts SBC after EBITDA, so ebitda_margin_path = TRI adjusted EBITDA margin + sbc_pct (the gross-up). Owner EBITDA therefore equals TRI's adjusted EBITDA less the ~0.2pp equity-award withholding tax. Base adjusted-margin path: 40.2% FY2026 (guided +100bp) rising to 44.0% by FY2032.
inputs.notes: MODEL: Owner-FCF DCF, component route, 10-year horizon (margins still expanding through ~year 7). Routing: an operating information-services and software company with no deposits, no fair-value property and no holdco discount, so the SKILL.md operating-company row applies, plus owner-fcf-adaptations for the CAD quote vs USD statements and IFRS 16 leases. This is the first valuation of this ticker, with no prior DCF or memory entry. BASE PERIOD: only FY2018 onward is comparable. The F&R (Refinitiv) sale halved revenue from $11,333M to $5,501M, and FY2018 and FY2021 net income are dominated by Refinitiv/LSEG gains, so net income and EPS are not used as anchors. The LSEG stake was fully sold in 2024 and its proceeds were returned in the May 2026 $605M return of capital, so it is NOT a bridge asset. FindLaw was disposed in Dec 2024 and is already out of the FY2025 base. TIMING: FY0 is FY2025 actual and year 1 is FY2026 discounted a full period. That is conservative by roughly three quarters of a year of discounting because FY2026 is ~80% elapsed; it matches the folder's end-of-year convention. NET DEBT: bonds plus commercial paper $2,941M less cash $577M at 30 Jun 2026 (Q2 2026 net-debt reconciliation, TRI.TO_Quarterly_Q2-2026.txt:1852), plus the $238M July 2026 buyback, which is already reflected in the 4 Aug share count and so has to be in the debt too. That gives $2,602M with leases excluded per treatment (B). BUYBACKS: TRI is a heavy repurchaser ($1,000M FY2025; $600M 2026 program completed in July at ~US$92-101/share) on top of a $2.62 dividend, so the flat share count is funded rather than a convention. INTEREST INCOME: not stripped, because TRI is net debt; interest income is $46M FY2025 and falling. FY0 CHECK: the component build on FY2025 ex-Print gives owner EBITDA ~$2.67bn, cash tax ~18%, capex 8% and D&A ~11.8%. That yields unlevered owner FCF of ~$1.75-1.85bn before deferred-revenue capture, against company FCF of $1.95bn (post net interest of ~$92M, pre equity-award tax), less the ~$0.1bn Print contribution. The two tie within working-capital noise.
inputs.fy2026_guidance: Raised Aug 2026 (Q2 report): total and organic revenue growth ~8.0% (from 7.5-8.0%); Big 3 9.5-10.0%; adjusted EBITDA margin +100bp vs 39.2%; FCF ~$2.1bn (still including Global Print; to be re-issued with Q3 on 3 Nov 2026); accrued capex ~8.0% of revenue; net interest expense $150-160M; adjusted ETR ~19%. Q3 2026 guide: organic ~8%, adjusted EBITDA margin ~36% (severance, M&A dilution, softer government).

equity_bridge.item: Global Print 51% sale: net cash proceeds
equity_bridge.note: ~$500M gross at Q4 2026 close (Q2 2026 Note 19, TRI.TO_Quarterly_Q2-2026.txt:4096) less ~$50M estimated tax on the pre-tax gain and deal costs. Global Print is excluded from the forward flows, so its value enters here.

The deal implies ~$480M for 49% (500/0.51 x 0.49). Haircut ~27% for the structurally declining print business (-3% to -6%/yr) and TRI's minimum-return backstop to KKR, a contingent liability that sits behind TRI's equity.

equity_bridge.item: Series II cumulative redeemable preference shares
equity_bridge.note: 6,000,000 shares, $110M stated capital (FY2025 note 25). A senior claim ahead of common equity.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_5yr_cagr (FY2020-FY2025, post-Refinitiv base). Equity CAGR is rejected as the primary because TRI returns >100% of FCF via dividends, buybacks and the 2026 return of capital, so book value does not compound with the business.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3yr CAGR (0.1%) and 5yr (3.6%) diverge >30% from revenue (4.1-4.6%), EPS (6.6-8.2%) and owner FCF (10-16%). The cause is capital return, not weakness. Reported revenue CAGRs also understate the underlying business: they are net of the FindLaw/non-core disposals and Global Print decline, and FY2025 organic growth was 7% vs 3% reported. Forward base growth (8.6% FY2026 ex-Print, decelerating) is anchored on the FY2026 guidance and the 8-11% Big 3 market growth, not on the historical reported CAGR.
historical_growth.notes: All CAGRs start at FY2020 or later and exclude the FY2015-FY2017 pre-separation years. EPS is GAAP and noisy (FY2021 $11.50 includes the LSEG gain, so it is excluded from the endpoints). Owner FCF = OCF - capex - SBC: FY2020 $1,177M, FY2022 $1,235M, FY2025 $1,906M. The SBC-adjusted FCF CAGR is in line with reported (SBC at ~1.5% of revenue is immaterial to the trend), though SBC itself grew 28% in FY2025 ($87M to $111M).

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 ex-Print = ~8.0% total guidance + ~0.65pp Global Print uplift. Deceleration to 4% by FY2035 sits inside the 8-11% Big 3 addressable-market growth early and converges toward nominal GDP plus pricing. Tuck-in M&A (~$0.3-0.6bn/yr) helps sustain this. Acquisition spend is not modelled as a separate outflow, so the late-year path is kept deliberately below the market-growth estimate.
base.margin_rationale: TRI adjusted EBITDA margin 39.4% ex-Print FY2025, +100bp guided FY2026, then +50-80bp/yr of operating leverage on a largely fixed cost base. It plateaus at 44.0%, roughly the FY2025 Big 3 margin of 43.6% plus modest leverage, held from FY2032. Engine margin = adjusted margin + SBC% (see inputs.ebitda_basis).
base.da_rationale: Software D&A guided $890-910M FY2026 (~11.7% of ex-Print revenue). It glides to 9% so that D&A converges on the 8% capex and the tax shield is not perpetuated above reinvestment.
base.tax_rationale: FY2025 cash taxes on continuing operations $275M (TRI.TO_Annual_FY2025.txt:5178); adjusted ETR guided ~19% FY2026. The rate ramps to 20% for Pillar Two and the HMRC DPT dispute.
base.wc_rationale: Prepaid subscriptions: deferred revenue rose $189M in FY2025 on ~$500M of organic revenue growth (~38%). 25% capture on the revenue change is used, haircut for billing-timing noise.

scenario_narratives.base: CoCounsel and the agentic Westlaw/Checkpoint/ONESOURCE releases are monetised as upsell into an embedded, 92%-retention installed base. Fiduciary-grade AI grounded in the proprietary corpus (KeyCite, the Key Number System, 1,500 attorney editors) holds pricing, so GenAI is net additive to wallet share rather than a substitute. Big 3 organic growth runs ~9.5-10% in FY2026 and fades toward market rates as AI pricing laps. Reuters is flat-to-down and Global Print is gone. Margin expands ~4.5pp over seven years on operating leverage, and capital return of >75% of FCF continues.
scenario_narratives.bull: AI becomes a pricing event, not a substitution event. CoCounsel tiers and consumption-based agentic products lift ARPU, international Big 3 expansion and tuck-ins (SafeSend, Additive, Noetica) compound, and Big 3 sustains ~10%+ organic growth through FY2029. Margin reaches ~46.5% adjusted (Big 3 economics plus a smaller Reuters drag), and the February 2026 AI selloff proves an overreaction, as it did for prior 'Westlaw is dead' scares.
scenario_narratives.bear: The Feb 2026 fear is realised. Foundation-model vendors (Anthropic's Claude legal tools), Harvey-style AI natives and the Global 7 accounting firms' in-house builds commoditise research and document review. Seat counts at law firms and corporate legal/tax departments compress as associate and preparer headcount falls, and renewals reprice down. FY2026 is largely locked in by the subscription book (~8%), but growth then drops to 2.5-3.5%. Margin gives back ~2pp to defensive AI investment and price concessions, capex rises to 8.5%, and Reuters keeps shrinking. The business survives as a cash-generative utility with a 14x exit multiple, and does not collapse.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25% because GenAI substitution of legal and tax research is a live, unresolved threat that the market priced hard in 2026 (52-week range C$107.91-230.00), and the evidence on CoCounsel monetisation is still early. Base 50% reflects the raised FY2026 guidance and Big 3 organic growth accelerating to 10% in Q2 2026, which show no sign of erosion yet. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs AI to be a pricing tailwind AND sustained double-digit Big 3 growth AND further margin expansion, three things going right at once.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF DCF on continuing operations excluding Global Print, with SBC fully expensed (TRI's adjusted EBITDA is already post-SBC) and the share count held flat because a heavy buyback programme funds it. Leases are an operating cost. AI-disruption risk is charged once, in the scenario flows and the 25% bear weight, not in WACC. Global Print is valued in the bridge at deal-implied value net of a backstop haircut. Values are computed in USD and converted to CAD for comparison with the TSX quote.
key_risks_to_valuation: GenAI disintermediation of Westlaw/Practical Law/Checkpoint research and drafting: the single largest swing factor, worth roughly the base-to-bear gap
Terminal value carries most of the value at 8.5% WACC and 3% terminal growth; a 1pp WACC move shifts value materially (see sensitivity grid)
The FY2026 outlook will be re-based at Q3 (3 Nov 2026) with Global Print as discontinued, and the Q3 adjusted EBITDA margin is guided down to ~36% on severance and M&A dilution
M&A dependence: part of the forward growth relies on tuck-in acquisitions whose spend is not modelled as a separate outflow
USD/CAD: the CAD-quoted value moves with the exchange rate even when USD fundamentals do not
Global Print minimum-return backstop to KKR is an unquantified contingent liability
